newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees $440 million from 1997 privatizations.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees $440 million from 1997 privatizations.

text.p: Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress Wednesday the government's budget estimated income from the sale of state assets next year would be $440 million.
"With respect to capital income, the amount 1.184 billion soles - equivalent to $440 million - has been budgeted," Camet said. "These revenues will come from the privatization of companies."
The government's 1996 budget estimated income from privatizations at $1 billion.
This was surpassed in the single sale earlier this year of a 26.6 state-held percent stake in Telefonica del Peru , which raised $1.25 billion.

Since 1992 the government has raised around $6.5 billion through the sale of state assets. The companies buying the assets have also been obliged to make investment commitments worth more than $7 billion.
The government has to raise around a further $1.5 billion in cash and investment commitments to reach its target of receiving $15 billion from its 1992-1998 privatization program.
